newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court rules for Bic Benelux on disposable razors.
newsitem.headline: Court rules for Bic Benelux on disposable razors.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Thursday Belgium's tax and labelling requirement on disposable razors sets a technical standard on goods subject to Community rules.

An obligation to mark products subject to an environmental tax falls within the Community's technical standards directive and requires member states to notify the European Commission before enacting such a rule.
Member states must justify the necessity of such rules, the court said.

Bic Benelux challenged a Belgian law which requires disposable razors to be marked and taxed at the rate of 10 Belgian francs each, arguing that Belgium failed to notify the Commission before enacting the rule.
The Belgian court asked for clarity as to whether labelling requirements fall within the directive's category of technical specifications.
Both the Belgian government and the Commission argued that the labelling requirements were environmental protection measures, but the court said the issue was one of trade.

"The aim of the directive is to protect the freedom of movement of goods...and such monitoring is necessary since technical regulations are capable of hindering, directly or indirectly, actually or potentially, intra-Community trade in goods," the court said.
Belgian law requires an environmental tax of 10 francs to be paid on all items that are used once, or a limited number of times, such as disposable razors.
"Technical regulations and specifications - Marking of products subject to environmental tax"
Reference from by the Belgian Conseil d'Etat for a preliminary ruling between

on the interpretation of article 1(1) and (5) Council directive 83/189/EEC of 28 March 1983 (OJ 1983 L 109, p.8) laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations, as amended by Council directive 88/182/EEC of 22 March 1988 (OJ 1988 L 81, p. 75)

An obligation to affix specific distinctive signs to products which are subject to tax levied on them on account of the environmental damage which they are deemed to cause, such as that laid down in articles 11 and 18 of the Ministerial Order of 24 December 1993 concerning the treatment of products subject to environmental tax, constitutes a technical specification within the meaning of Council directive 83/189/EEC of 28 March 1983 laying down a procedure for the provision of information in the field of technical standards and regulations, as amended by Council directived 88/182/EEC of 22 March 1988, and the national enactment introducing it is a technical regulation within the meaning of the same directive.
